issue.title: fix(inbox): sanitize unpaired UTF-16 surrogates in DM bubbles
issue.body:
## Summary

- Adds `StringUtils.sanitizeUtf16` — strips unpaired UTF-16 surrogate code units, returns the same instance when input is already well-formed
- Applies it once at the top of `MessageBubble.build` so substring/split and the downstream `Text` widget all see clean input
- New unit tests for the sanitizer and a widget test asserting `MessageBubble` doesn't crash on an unpaired surrogate

## Why

NIP-17 rumor bodies and other sender-controlled text reach the app via JSON `\uXXXX` escapes that can carry unpaired surrogates. Strict UTF-8 in the local nip44 path catches byte-level malformations, but JSON-decoded escape sequences slip through. Flutter's text renderer asserts well-formed UTF-16 and crashes with `Invalid argument(s): string is not well-formed UTF-16`, taking out the open conversation. Surfaced in production logs after PR #4451 made the inbox usable on staging.

Closes #4463.

## Test plan

- [x] `flutter test test/utils/string_utils_test.dart` — 8 sanitizer cases (ASCII identity, empty identity, emoji preserved, unpaired high/low/trailing dropped, valid pairs around unpaired)
- [x] `flutter test test/screens/inbox/conversation/widgets/message_bubble_test.dart` — 29 cases incl. new surrogate-doesn't-crash assertion
- [x] `flutter analyze` clean on the three changed files

issue.title: Notifications: refresh auth, support stable cursors, and speed comment targets
issue.body:
## Problem
The notifications flow has multiple regressions around Funnelcake integration and notification target routing:

- NIP-98 auth events can be reused beyond Funnelcake's 60-second freshness window, causing notification pagination requests to fail when a cached token ages out.
- Funnelcake notification pagination now returns stable cursor pairs, but the mobile client does not consistently parse `next_cursor_id` or send `before_id` on follow-up requests.
- Tapping comment and reply notifications waits on target resolution work before navigating, which makes the interaction feel slow even when the destination can already be inferred.
- Notification target resolution should prefer uppercase `A` root addressable tags when present so comment notifications resolve to stable NIP-33 video routes instead of older event IDs.
- Explicit cursor overrides must win over stored cursor state so pagination does not accidentally reuse a stale `before_id`.

## Goal
Make notification pagination and deep linking reliable again by refreshing auth in time, supporting stable cursor pagination semantics, and reducing perceived latency when opening comment-related notifications.

## Scope
- Refresh or reissue NIP-98 auth before Funnelcake rejects a request for token age.
- Parse and persist stable notification cursor pairs, including `next_cursor_id`.
- Send `before_id` on subsequent notification page requests when the server provides a stable cursor pair.
- Navigate into comment and reply targets immediately, then complete target loading inside the opened screen.
- Prefer uppercase `A` root addressable tags in the notification resolver when present.
- Preserve explicit cursor override behavior so overrides do not silently fall back to stored pagination state.
- Remove any now-blocking analyzer noise directly related to the touched code path.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Notification pagination continues working when previously cached auth would have exceeded Funnelcake's 60-second freshness requirement.
- Follow-up notification page requests send the correct stable cursor fields expected by Funnelcake.
- Comment and reply notification taps show the destination route immediately instead of waiting for resolver work to finish first.
- Notifications that include an uppercase `A` root addressable tag resolve to the stable video route derived from that tag.
- Passing an explicit cursor override does not reuse a stored `before_id` from prior pagination state.
- Regression coverage exists for auth freshness, notification cursor parsing, repository pagination behavior, resolver routing, and notification tap navigation.

## Context
- Related backend work: divinevideo/divine-funnelcake#400
- This work is focused on reliability and responsiveness in the mobile notifications experience.

issue.title: feat(divine_video_player): add Linux platform support
issue.body:
## Goal

Extend the `divine_video_player` package (`mobile/packages/divine_video_player`) with Linux support so videos can be played on Linux desktop.

## Scope

- Register Linux as a supported platform in the package (`pubspec.yaml`, `platforms:` section).
- Integrate a suitable backend player for Linux — document the decision as part of the implementation.
- Adapt `DivineVideoPlayerController` and related widgets to work on Linux (initialization, play/pause/seek, buffering, disposal).

## Tests

- Run unit/widget tests for the controller on Linux.
- Manual smoke test: HLS and MP4 playback, seeking, volume, lifecycle (dispose).

## Out of Scope

- Hardware decoding tuning.
- Picture-in-Picture / fullscreen-specific Linux integrations (separate task if needed).

## Notes

- Check native libraries (e.g. `libfontconfig`, `libass`) for signing/loading similar to macOS (see `ffmpeg-kit-macos-codesign-crash` skill).
- Codesigning does not apply on Linux, but document dependency setup cleanly in the README.

issue.body:
## Goal

Extend the `divine_video_player` package (`mobile/packages/divine_video_player`) with Web support so videos can be played in Flutter Web.

## Scope

- Register Web as a supported platform in the package (`pubspec.yaml`, `platforms:` section).
- Integrate a web backend (e.g. `video_player_web` via `package:video_player`, or a `media_kit` web variant via `hls.js`). Document the decision as part of the implementation.
- Make `DivineVideoPlayerController` and widgets web-compatible:
  - HLS playback (via `hls.js` or native Safari HLS).
  - Direct MP4 playback.
  - Correct handling of `HtmlElementView` / platform views.
  - Respect autoplay policies (muted autoplay).

## Tests

- Web-specific widget tests where useful (`flutter test --platform chrome`).
- Manual smoke test in Chrome + Safari: HLS, MP4, seeking, lifecycle, multiple players on one page.

## Out of Scope

- PiP / Fullscreen API integration (separate task if needed).
- Casting / AirPlay.

## Notes

- Review existing web-specific player workarounds in `divine-mobile` (`mobile/lib/...`) — some may move into the package.
- Mind the `proxy-range-header-forwarding` and `http-video-streaming-headers` skills — the web player is sensitive to Range/Content-Range headers.

issue.title: Inbox: 'Invalid argument(s): string is not well-formed UTF-16' renders DM/notification text
issue.body:
## Symptoms

While the Inbox tab is open, the app logs Flutter framework errors:

```
[SYSTEM] Flutter Error: Invalid argument(s): string is not well-formed UTF-16
Flutter framework error: Invalid argument(s): string is not well-formed UTF-16
```

Observed 3 times in a single session on staging while the inbox was visible (logs at 17:14:52, 17:15:04, 17:15:23).

## Timing evidence (points at DM, not notifications)

Each occurrence is immediately preceded by a batch of `nip44_decrypt` RPC calls:

```
[Keycast RPC] nip44_decrypt completed in 378ms (HTTP 200)
[Keycast RPC] Calling nip44_decrypt...
[Keycast RPC] nip44_decrypt completed in 394ms (HTTP 200)
[17:15:04.609] [SYSTEM] Flutter Error: Invalid argument(s): string is not well-formed UTF-16
```

The notification REST path (`/api/users/:pk/notifications`) is plain JSON — no nip44 involved. The clustering with `nip44_decrypt` strongly suggests this fires from **DM conversation rendering** (decrypted message previews / message bubbles), not the notification list.

## Likely root cause

A Dart `String` is being constructed from decrypted bytes (likely via `utf8.decode(..., allowMalformed: true)` somewhere in the nip44 decrypt path), which can produce strings containing **unpaired UTF-16 surrogates**. Flutter's text engine then throws when it tries to render them.

## Candidate code paths to investigate

- `mobile/lib/screens/inbox/conversation/widgets/message_bubble.dart` — message text rendering
- `mobile/lib/screens/inbox/conversation/conversation_view.dart`
- The keycast nip44 decrypt boundary — wherever decrypted bytes become a Dart `String`. Check whether bytes are decoded with `allowMalformed: true` and not subsequently sanitized.

## Suggested fix shape

At the decrypt → String boundary, sanitize unpaired surrogates, e.g.:

```dart
String sanitizeUtf16(String input) =>
    String.fromCharCodes(input.runes); // drops unpaired surrogates
```

This is a band-aid at the rendering boundary — the better fix is to ensure the decrypt path never produces a malformed string in the first place (treat bytes as UTF-8 strictly, log + skip the message if it fails).

## Reproduction

Open the Inbox tab on staging with a logged-in user that has at least one DM conversation. The errors fire shortly after the inbox loads and decrypts message previews.

## Not the cause (already ruled out)

- `mobile/lib/notifications/widgets/notification_actor_spans.dart` uses `indexOf` + `substring` on the same string. Those cuts are always on UTF-16 code-unit boundaries by construction, so they can't split a surrogate pair unless the input already contains an unpaired surrogate — i.e. this widget is at most a victim, not a source.

## Surfaced by

Diagnostic logging added in #4451 (notification fetch error context), which made the inbox-load failure path visible in the same session.

issue.title: fix(notifications): refresh auth and stable cursors
issue.body:
Closes #4452

## Summary
- Shorten NIP-98 auth token caching to stay inside Funnelcake's 60s freshness window and make token time checks clock-driven for regression coverage.
- Add mobile support for Funnelcake notification stable cursor pairs: parse next_cursor_id and send before_id on subsequent pages.
- Speed comment/reply notification taps by pushing the fullscreen route before the relay resolver completes, while the opened screen loads the target video.
- Prefer NIP-22 uppercase A root addressable tags in the notification resolver, so comment notifications can fetch stable NIP-33 video routes instead of stale event IDs when available.
- Preserve Liz's cursor override fix so explicit cursor overrides do not accidentally reuse a stored before_id.
- Add Funnelcake notification fetch diagnostics: failed fetch exceptions now include request URL/cursor params, response body, and correlation headers such as x-request-id/traceparent/cf-ray when present.
- Remove a redundant infinite_video_feed default argument that blocked full analyzer.

## Context
- Related backend PR: divinevideo/divine-funnelcake#400
- Fixes the notification pagination path reusing a cached NIP-98 event after Funnelcake rejects events older than 60s.
- The slow comment tap log showed route navigation waiting on resolver work before /pooled-video-feed appeared; the UI now navigates immediately for reply/comment-like targets and keeps mention profile fallback behavior unchanged.
- A bare `500 {"error":"Internal server error"}` from notifications is not enough to debug backend failures; the next client log will include the exact signed request URL and any edge/backend correlation headers available on the response.

Closes #4459

Reverts divinevideo/divine-mobile#4404

This PR changes the default value for **every** `DivineVideoPlayer` back to the old Android legacy surface. We already know that the old surface causes issues in the video editor, which is exactly why we moved away from it before. We only need the old surface in the feed for now, because otherwise there is flickering between video players until the Flutter team fixes that issue.

Switching every video player back to the legacy surface just reintroduces problems we already fixed.

@realmeylisdev I tested this on my Samsung Galaxy and I was not able to reproduce the issue before or after this change. Were you able to reproduce it on a real device and verify that this actually fixes it? 
Because I’m pretty sure this would not solve the issue at all, especially since we never shipped the new surface to production users yet so the fix undo something which users never had in the play-store version. That would mean somebody internally must have experienced this issue that we see it in Crashlytics.

issue.title: fix(push): send push control events to Divine relay with relay OK handling
issue.body:
## Summary
Mobile push control events need to reliably reach the Divine relay path consumed by `divine-push-service` so real FCM push registration, deregistration, and preference updates work in production.

## Context
Recent investigation found:

- PR #4162 fixes the signer-readiness race by delaying registration until a signer-backed Nostr session is ready.
- A prod-emulator test showed generic relay-pool publishing could report success while the kind `3079` event landed on a user relay (`nos.lol`) instead of `relay.divine.video`.
- A targeted diagnostic run against `wss://relay.divine.video` showed the relay rejected `3079` with `blocked: kind 3079 not in allowed list`.
- Relay-side allowlist/discovery work is tracked in `divine-funnelcake#380`.
- First-party mobile does not publish kind `1` events today.
- Mobile consumes kind `1` for mention-style notifications.
- Mobile comments/replies are currently published as kind `1111`.
- This issue should not expand mobile push preferences to `1111` or `30023`.

## Scope
- Publish push control events directly to `EnvironmentConfig.relayUrl`.
- Await NIP-20 relay `OK` for push control events.
- Use a bounded `5s` relay OK timeout.
- Log relay outcomes:
  - `acceptedBy`
  - `rejectedBy`
  - `noResponseFrom`
- Apply targeted relay + OK behavior to:
  - `3079` push registration.
  - `3080` push deregistration.
  - `3083` push preferences.
- Preserve the readiness-driven registration lifecycle from PR #4162.
- Preserve token-refresh re-registration behavior, but make refreshed-token registration use the same targeted relay + OK path.
- Keep `p` tags targeting `EnvironmentConfig.pushServicePubkey`.
- Keep existing `NotificationPreferences` trigger kind list unchanged for now: `[1, 3, 7, 16]`.
- Add temporary relay-layer diagnostics for push control kinds `3079/3080/3083` during rollout.
- Keep permanent push-control logs in `PushNotificationService`.
- Do not add a durable retry/background scheduler in this issue.

## Current Mobile Kind Contract Notes
- `1`: consumed for mention-style notifications; not first-party published by mobile; not current comments/replies.
- `3`: follows/contact-list.
- `7`: likes/reactions.
- `16`: generic reposts.
- `1111`: current mobile comments/replies, but not yet advertised in `3083` preferences.
- `30023`: mobile can consume long-form mentions locally, but not yet advertised in `3083` preferences.

## Out of Scope
- Adding `1111` to mobile push preferences.
- Adding `30023` to mobile push preferences.
- Changing canonical notification trigger-kind policy.
- Adding relay-side allowlist changes.
- Adding durable retry queues or background retry scheduling.
- Hardening relay policy to require `p` tags for push control kinds.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `3079` registration targets `EnvironmentConfig.relayUrl` and awaits/logs relay OK/reject/no-response.
- [ ] Token-refresh registration uses the same targeted relay + OK handling.

- [ ] Push control publishes use a bounded `5s` relay OK timeout.

- [ ] No new durable retry/background scheduler is introduced.
- [ ] Temporary relay-layer diagnostics are limited to push control kinds `3079/3080/3083`.

  - Confirm logs show target relay, relay OK result, and push-service processing evidence.

## Dependencies
- Depends on `divine-funnelcake#380` or equivalent deployment allowing push control kinds on `relay.divine.video`:
  - `3079`
  - `3080`
  - `3083`
- `divine-funnelcake#380` should also advertise newly allowed control kinds in discovery metadata.

issue.title: fix(push): send push control events to Divine relay with relay OK handling
issue.body:
## Summary

Push registration could look successful even when the Divine relay never accepted the event.
This change sends push registration, deregistration, and preference events directly to the configured Divine relay and waits for a relay OK response.
It also keeps the publish bounded so a late relay connection cannot write or queue a stale push-control event after the timeout.

## What Changed

Push control events now use the same targeted OK-confirmed publish path.
The relay layer now treats the caller timeout as one deadline for both sending and waiting for OK responses.
Same-URL fallback now distinguishes a failed send from a sent frame, and deadline-bound sends cannot queue stale EVENT messages.

- Route kinds 3079, 3080, and 3083 through `publishEventAwaitOk` with `targetRelays: [EnvironmentConfig.relayUrl]`.
- Let explicit target-relay OK publishes run even when the general relay pool has no connected relays.
- Skip the generic disconnected-relay retry when explicit target relays are provided.
- Bound `RelayPool.sendEventAwaitOk` with one deadline across `_sendCollect` plus OK waiting.
- Thread that deadline through `Relay.send`, `RelayBase.send`, and `WebSocketConnectionManager.sendJson`.
- Disable pending-message queueing for deadline-bound await-OK sends.
- Do not queue pending-auth messages for deadline-bound await-OK sends.
- Remove expired temp relays after deadline timeout so their connection waiters cannot flush stale control events.
- Track expected relays as soon as each send succeeds, so timeouts report the relays that actually received the frame.
- Avoid retrying a stalled same-URL normal target as a temp relay after the shared deadline is consumed.
- Allow same-URL temp fallback when the normal target path returns `false` immediately without sending.
- Log accepted, rejected, and no-response relay outcomes without logging encrypted push-control content.

**Related Issue:** Closes #4411

## Testing

I tested the push-control service paths, the client OK-publish wrapper, and the relay-pool timeout and fallback behavior.
I also verified the touched packages and the app analyzer after the SDK API change.

- `dart format packages/nostr_client/lib/src/nostr_client.dart packages/nostr_client/test/src/nostr_client_test.dart packages/nostr_sdk/lib/relay/relay_pool.dart packages/nostr_sdk/test/unit/relay_pool_concurrency_test.dart`
- `dart format --output=none --set-exit-if-changed lib/relay/relay.dart lib/relay/relay_base.dart lib/relay/relay_isolate.dart lib/relay/web_socket_connection_manager.dart lib/relay/relay_pool.dart test/unit/relay_pool_concurrency_test.dart test/unit/relay_pool_auth_test.dart test/unit/relay_count_test.dart test/integration/relay_auth_test.dart test/integration/nip50_search_test.dart`
- `dart format --output=none --set-exit-if-changed test/src/follow_repository_test.dart`
- `flutter test --no-pub test/src/nostr_client_test.dart --plain-name "publishEventAwaitOk"`
- `flutter test --no-pub test/unit/relay_pool_concurrency_test.dart --plain-name "sendEventAwaitOk"`
- `flutter test --no-pub test/unit/relay_pool_concurrency_test.dart`
- `dart test test/unit/publish_outcome_test.dart`
- `flutter test --no-pub test/services/push_notification_service_test.dart`
- `flutter test --no-pub test/providers/push_notification_sync_test.dart`
- `dart analyze` in `mobile/packages/nostr_sdk`
- `flutter analyze --no-pub` in `mobile/packages/nostr_client`
- `flutter analyze --no-pub` in `mobile/packages/follow_repository`
- `flutter analyze --no-pub` in `mobile`
- `flutter test --no-pub` in `mobile`
- `git diff --check`

## Risks

The main behavior change is that explicit target publishes no longer wait for unrelated pool reconnects, and deadline-bound OK publishes no longer queue messages for later delivery.
That is intentional for push control events because a late queued control event can make the app report a failed publish while still mutating relay-side push state later.
The SDK `Relay.send` interface now accepts an optional deadline, so custom test relays and package-local fake relays were updated to match.

- A target URL already present in the normal relay pool is not retried as a temp relay after the normal path sends or queues the frame.
- A normal target path that returns `false` immediately can still fall back to a same-URL temp relay within the caller timeout.
- If the normal target path stalls until the shared deadline is exhausted, the publish fails fast instead of trying the same URL a second way.
- If a relay connects after the deadline, the deadline-aware send path returns false before writing the stale EVENT.
- This does not prove the push service processed the event after relay acceptance; it only confirms relay acceptance.

## Type of Change

- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [x] 🛠️ Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] ❌ Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)
- [ ] 🧹 Code refactor
- [ ] ✅ Build configuration change

issue.title: Notifications: prefer human-readable actors in grouped rows
issue.body:
## Problem
Grouped notification rows can surface the wrong lead actor when the newest actor does not have a useful human-readable display name.

Current behavior can show:
- a hash-like actor name instead of a recognizable display name
- `Unknown user` as the lead actor even when another grouped actor has a valid explicit name

That makes grouped notification rows harder to scan and lowers confidence in who actually triggered the notification.

## Goal
Prefer a human-readable actor name for grouped notification rows so the most visible actor label is informative and consistent with the existing generated display-name fallback behavior.

## Scope
- Choose an explicitly named actor as the lead actor when grouped notification data includes one.
- Fall back to the existing generated display-name behavior when the newest actor name is hash-like or otherwise not suitable for display.
- Preserve the current grouped notification behavior outside actor-name selection.
- Add regression coverage for grouped notifications where the newest actor has a hash-like name and another actor has a better explicit display name.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Grouped notification rows prefer an actor with a useful explicit display name over a newer actor whose display name is hash-like.
- `Unknown user` is not shown as the lead actor when a valid named actor is available in the grouped row.
- Existing display-name fallback behavior remains intact for actors without usable names.
- Regression tests cover grouped notification ordering and actor-name selection for the hash-like-name case.

## Context
This work is focused on improving notification readability without changing the underlying notification grouping model.
